title: Reading Errors, Asking Useful Debugging Questions and Saving Versions
learningObjectives: Explain the difference between syntax errors, runtime errors and logic errors, using simple examples.
Read an error message and identify the likely file, line, error type and useful diagnostic details.
Reproduce a problem consistently and record the actions and conditions that cause it.
Compare the expected result with the actual result to describe the problem precisely.
Use the first relevant error message as a clue and inspect the nearby code without assuming it always identifies the root cause.
Use the browser developer tools and code editor diagnostics to gather evidence about a problem.
Change one small thing at a time, test again and observe whether the result improves or changes.
Ask a useful debugging question that includes the expected result, actual result, reproduction steps and exact error text.
Share only the smallest relevant code sample and enough context for another person to understand the issue.
Remove passwords, API keys, access tokens and personal information before sharing logs or code publicly.
Save named backup copies and explain how version control records changes over time.
Restore a previously working version safely and verify that the restored project behaves as expected.

understand.concept: An error is information that something did not work as expected. A syntax error breaks the writing rules of a language. A runtime error happens while a program is running. A logic error allows the program to run but produces an incorrect result. Debugging is the evidence-based process of reproducing a problem, investigating its cause, making a controlled correction and testing again.
understand.whyItMatters: Debug systematically: reproduce the problem, read the first useful error message, note the file and line, inspect nearby code, change one thing at a time and test again. A useful debugging question explains what you expected, what actually happened, how to reproduce it, the smallest relevant code sample and the exact error text. Remove secrets before sharing anything. Save working versions or use version control so you can recover a known-good state.
understand.history: This lesson focuses on current, practical web-development concepts; historical claims are omitted where they are not needed.
understand.analogy: Debugging is like tracing a fault in a machine by checking one component at a time. The analogy has limits: software behaviour can depend on state, timing, environment and inputs. Record the conditions that reproduce the issue. Save named versions or use version control so a working state can be restored.

examples.explanation: Create a small intentional error in a practice project. Reproduce it, read the first useful console or editor message, record the file and line, inspect the relevant code, change one thing and test again. Write a short report with Expected, Actual, Steps to reproduce, Error, Relevant code and Fix. Never include passwords or private API keys.
examples.expectedOutput: A clear debugging report and a safely saved working version.

practise.guidedTask: Create a small intentional error in a practice project. Reproduce it, read the first useful console or editor message, record the file and line, inspect the relevant code, change one thing and test again. Write a short report with Expected, Actual, Steps to reproduce, Error, Relevant code and Fix. Never include passwords or private API keys.
practise.independentTask: మీరు ఎదుర్కొన్న లేదా ఉద్దేశపూర్వకంగా సృష్టించిన ఒక Bug కోసం Debugging Report తయారు చేయండి. Expected Result, Actual Result, Reproduction Steps, Exact Error, Relevant Code, Fix, Saved Version వివరాలు చేర్చండి. రహస్య సమాచారాన్ని తొలగించండి.
hints: సమస్యను మళ్లీ ఉత్పత్తి చేయగలిగేలా చర్యలను నమోదు చేయండి.
మొదటి ఉపయోగకరమైన Error Message, File Name, Line Number గమనించండి.
ఒకేసారి ఒక మార్పు చేసి మళ్లీ పరీక్షించండి.
Passwordలు, API Keys, Access Tokens పంచుకోకండి.
పనిచేసిన Version‌ను Backup లేదా Version Control‌లో భద్రపరచండి.
